-- UIParent.lua l.14-42: UIPanelWindows["FrameName"] = { area, pushable, whileDead }. Only the -- rows benilla ships/anticipates today (pin §1): Gossip + Merchant are live; Loot registers -- now (pushable=7) so the coming loot window lands on an already-wired system. UIPanelWindows = {} UIPanelWindows["GossipFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["MerchantFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The mail window (decision 0544): the reference UIParent.lua l.37 registers MailFrame -- area="left", pushable=0. The OpenMailFrame is NOT a panel — it is a special-frame toplevel -- (UIParent.lua l.46 UISpecialFrames), closed by ESC in ToggleGameMenu below. Our own -- escapable toplevels stay hard-listed in that chain rather than pushed into -- UISpecialFrames — the table exists now (1206) but it is the ADDONS' list, and mixing our -- windows into it would make an addon's `tremove` able to break the client's own ESC. UIPanelWindows["MailFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The trade window (decision 0592 P1, TradeFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.27 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["TradeFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 1 }`). Without -- this row ShowUIPanel takes its unregistered branch — a bare frame:Show() with no left-slot -- placement — so the window flips IsShown() but never lands on screen (the bug: OPEN_WINDOW -- arrived on both clients, yet no window). pushable=1 lets a pushable=0 panel (a merchant) -- shove it to center, the reference's browse-while-trading arbitration. UIPanelWindows["TradeFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 1 } -- The trainer window (decision 0237 phase 3, TrainerFrame.xml): an NPC session exactly like -- Gossip/Merchant above (area "left", pushable 0) — competes for/replaces them at the slot. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTrainerFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The bank window (decision 0604 phase 4, BankFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.28 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["BankFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 }`), quoted -- verbatim — the same left-slot competition as the other NPC-session windows above. UIPanelWindows["BankFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 } -- The taxi-map window (decision 0484 phase 2, TaxiFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua -- registration line (`UIPanelWindows["TaxiFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 }`), -- quoted verbatim — same left-slot competition as Gossip/Merchant/Trainer above. UIPanelWindows["TaxiFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The dressing room (decision 1060, DressUpFrame.xml): the ref's own UIParent.lua l.41 -- registration (`UIPanelWindows["DressUpFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 2 }`), quoted -- verbatim — pushable=2 lets the NPC-session windows (pushable=0) shove it aside, which is -- what makes "ctrl-click a merchant's item" show both. UIPanelWindows["DressUpFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 2 } UIPanelWindows["QuestFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["QuestLogFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } UIPanelWindows["LootFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 7 } -- The character window (decision 0208 phase 1a, CharacterFrame.xml): the ref's own -- CharacterFrame row (area "left", pushable 0) — competes for/replaces the other left-slot -- windows exactly like Gossip/Merchant/Quest/QuestLog above. UIPanelWindows["CharacterFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The inspect window (decision 0631, InspectFrame.xml): the ref's own InspectFrame row -- (`Blizzard_InspectUI.lua:4` — area "left", pushable 0), so inspecting swaps out whichever -- left-slot window was open, exactly as the character window does. UIPanelWindows["BenillaInspectFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The spellbook (decision 0216 §8, SpellBookFrame.xml): the ref's own SpellBookFrame row -- (area "left", pushable 0) — same left-slot competition as every window above. UIPanelWindows["SpellBookFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0 } -- The talent window (decision 0304 §4, TalentFrame.xml): the ref's own TalentFrame row is -- `{ area = "left", pushable = 6, whileDead = 1 }` — pushable 6 kept (one tier above the -- plain NPC-session/player-state windows' 0, matching the ref exactly); `whileDead` is -- OMITTED like every other row here (none of them model it, even though ShowUIPanel's own -- guard already reads `info.whileDead` — ShowUIPanel's own comment: `UnitIsDead` doesn't -- exist yet, so the guard is inert either way today). UIPanelWindows["BenillaTalentFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 6 } -- The social window (decision 0668) — the ref's own registration line verbatim -- (`UIPanelWindows["FriendsFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 }`, -- UIParent.lua l.29). whileDead: a corpse run is exactly when you want to whisper someone. UIPanelWindows["FriendsFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- The macro window (decision 0983, MacroFrame.xml) — the ref's own registration line -- verbatim (`UIPanelWindows["MacroFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 5, whileDead = 1 }`, -- Blizzard_MacroUI.lua:7). whileDead is the ref's and it earns its keep: writing a macro -- during a corpse run is a real thing people do. UIPanelWindows["BenillaMacroFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 5, whileDead = 1 } -- The crafting window (decision 0437 phase 2, TradeSkillFrame.xml): NOT an NPC session (it -- opens off your own cast, TradeSkillFrame.xml's own header comment) — the ref Lua's own -- registration line (Blizzard_TradeSkillUI.lua:13) is `{ area = "left", pushable = 3 }`, -- quoted verbatim. UIPanelWindows["BenillaTradeSkillFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 3 } -- The Enchanting window (decision 0437 phase 3, CraftFrame.xml): the ref Lua's own -- registration line (`Blizzard_CraftUI.lua:24`), quoted verbatim — `pushable = 4`, NOT `3` -- (grepped both ref files directly to confirm: `3` is TradeSkillFrame's own line-13 value, -- a different window/depth — CraftFrame.xml's own header comment has the same note). UIPanelWindows["BenillaCraftFrame"] = { area = "left", pushable = 4 } -- The game menu (decision 0674, GameMenuFrame.xml) — the ref's own registration line -- verbatim (`UIPanelWindows["GameMenuFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, -- whileDead = 1 }`, UIParent.lua l.15), and the FIRST **center**-area row benilla ships. -- "center" is not a position here, it is a MODE: a native-center frame takes the center -- slot keeping its own anchor (the menu is screen-CENTER by its own XML), closes every -- other window on the way in, and — while it holds the slot — makes ShowUIPanel refuse -- every non-center panel (`CanOpenPanels` below). That is the rule behind "you can't open -- anything with the ESC menu up". whileDead: dying is exactly when you want to log out. UIPanelWindows["GameMenuFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- The options window (decision 0950, OptionsFrame.xml) — the ref's own registration -- verbatim (`UIPanelWindows["OptionsFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, -- whileDead = 1 }`, UIParent.lua l.16): the second native-center row. Same MODE as the -- menu above — it takes the screen, and dying is exactly when you might want to retune -- the client. (The ref's l.17-18 register SoundOptionsFrame/UIOptionsFrame the same way; -- those panels are this one window's category rows now, so the rows have no frames.) UIPanelWindows["OptionsFrame"] = { area = "center", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 } -- (0997's KeyBindingFrame row is gone — decision 1008 folded key bindings into the -- options window above, the 1.15 layout's own placement; KeyBindingsPage.xml.) -- The world map (decision 0203 phase 2) — the ref's own line verbatim (UIParent.lua l.30) -- and the first **full** row. It was a plain toplevel until now, showing itself with a bare -- `WorldMapFrame:Show()` and so bypassing this manager entirely: with the game menu up it -- was the ONE window that still opened (director-reported). Routing its toggle through -- ShowUIPanel is what subjects it to the same rules as everything else. UIPanelWindows["WorldMapFrame"] = { area = "full", pushable = 0, whileDead = 1 }
-- The real client stores `.left`/`.center`/`.doublewide`/`.fullscreen` as fields directly on -- the `UIParent` frame table (UIParent.lua l.789-885). benilla has no `UIParent` frame object -- yet (a later decision's job) — so the two slots this v1 tracks live in a private chunk-local -- table instead of squatting the `UIParent` global name; a future `CreateFrame("Frame", -- "UIParent")` then lands cleanly on an empty global rather than silently coexisting with our -- state. Every function below is defined in this same chunk, so they all close over it. local slots = { left = nil, center = nil, fullscreen = nil }
-- SetLeftFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.809-824. Hides the old left occupant, SetPoints + -- Shows the new one at the left slot's screen anchor (verified: TOPLEFT UIParent, 0, -104). -- "UIParent" as the relativeTo name doesn't resolve to a real frame yet (none exists) — the -- engine's SetPoint falls back to the frame's own parent-or-screen default, which for our -- top-level panel frames IS the screen root, so this already anchors correctly; the string is -- kept for fidelity/forward-compat with the day a real UIParent frame lands. function SetLeftFrame(frame) local oldFrame = slots.left slots.left = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) frame:Show() end end
-- SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) — UIParent.lua l.826-850. The `UIChildWindows` hide loop -- (l.840-846) is dropped: no such frames exist in benilla yet (out of v1 scope). function SetCenterFrame(frame, skipSetPoint) local oldFrame = slots.center slots.center = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:Show() if not skipSetPoint then frame:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) end end end
-- MovePanelToLeft() — UIParent.lua l.868-875: the center occupant slides back to the left slot -- (used when the left slot vacates and a "left-area" frame is holding center). function MovePanelToLeft() if slots.center then SetLeftFrame(nil) slots.center:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 0, -104) slots.left = slots.center slots.center = nil end end
-- MovePanelToCenter() — UIParent.lua l.877-885: the left occupant slides to the center slot -- (used when a higher-`pushable` frame wants the left spot). `:Raise()` (l.881) has no benilla -- frame-level equivalent yet — guarded, same posture as the pin's `UnitIsDead` guard below. function MovePanelToCenter() if slots.left then SetCenterFrame(nil) slots.left:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "UIParent", "TOPLEFT", 384, -104) if slots.left.Raise then slots.left:Raise() end slots.center = slots.left slots.left = nil end end
-- GetLeftFrame / GetCenterFrame — UIParent.lua l.916-922. function GetLeftFrame() return slots.left end
function GetCenterFrame() return slots.center end
-- SetFullScreenFrame(frame) — UIParent.lua l.852-866. ONE line dropped: the reference also -- does `UIParent:Hide()`/`:Show()` around the swap, hiding the whole game UI behind the -- fullscreen frame. benilla has no UIParent frame (the note on `slots` above), and the only -- full frame we ship — the world map — already paints its own full-screen blackout -- (WorldMapFrame.xml), which is what that Hide buys the reference. function SetFullScreenFrame(frame) local oldFrame = slots.fullscreen slots.fullscreen = frame if oldFrame then oldFrame:Hide() end if frame then frame:Show() end end
function GetFullScreenFrame() return slots.fullscreen end
-- CanOpenPanels() — UIParent.lua l.887-910. Its dead-player arms are commented out in the -- reference itself (both of them, with the note that the fear/out-of-control gate was -- "previously"); what survives is one rule: **a native-center frame open ⇒ nothing else -- opens**. The game menu is the only such frame (decision 0674), so this reads: with the -- ESC menu up, no window opens — not from a keybind, not from an NPC's OPEN_WINDOW. function CanOpenPanels() local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if not centerFrame then return 1 end local info = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if info and info.area == "center" then return nil end return 1 end
-- ShowUIPanel(frame) — UIParent.lua l.649-751, the left+center slice (pin §3 steps 1,3-5) -- plus the native-center mode decision 0674 needed. Still skipped by scope: full-screen -- (l.668-675, l.692-696 — no `full` row is registered; benilla's world map is a plain -- toplevel, not a panel) and `doublewide` (l.707-710 — likewise none). function ShowUIPanel(frame, force) if not frame or frame:IsVisible() then return end
local info = UIPanelWindows[frame:GetName()] -- l.655-657. Note the reference's own precedence: an UNREGISTERED frame is not gated -- (the `info and` term), so a bare toplevel still shows with the menu up. if not CanOpenPanels() and info and info.area ~= "center" then return end if not info then frame:Show() return end
-- UnitIsDead doesn't exist yet (pin §3) — guarded rather than assumed absent-forever. if type(UnitIsDead) == "function" and UnitIsDead("player") and not info.whileDead then return end
-- l.668-675: a full-screen frame open ignores every non-full open request (`force` -- evicts it instead). The world map is the only `full` row, so this reads: nothing opens -- behind the map. if GetFullScreenFrame() and info.area ~= "full" then if force then SetFullScreenFrame(nil) else return end end
-- l.677-689: with a native-center frame open, only another center request gets through -- — `force` evicts it instead of refusing. Redundant with the CanOpenPanels gate above -- for every caller that doesn't force (the reference double-checks it too); kept because -- it is the ONLY path that can displace the menu, and dropping it would silently turn -- `force` into a no-op. No benilla caller passes `force` yet. local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if centerFrame then local centerInfo = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if centerInfo and centerInfo.area == "center" and info.area ~= "center" then if force then SetCenterFrame(nil) else return end end end
-- l.692-696: full-screen frames just replace each other, and they take everything with -- them on the way in. if info.area == "full" then CloseAllWindows() SetFullScreenFrame(frame) return end
-- l.697-702: native-center frames just replace each other and take the screen — -- everything else closes first. `skipSetPoint` is the load-bearing argument: the menu -- keeps its own CENTER anchor instead of being dropped at the left-area seat. if info.area == "center" then CloseWindows() CloseAllBags() SetCenterFrame(frame, 1) return end
if info.area ~= "left" then -- No full/doublewide row is registered — defensive fallback only. frame:Show() return end
-- Try to put it on the left (l.719-723). local leftFrame = GetLeftFrame() if not leftFrame then SetLeftFrame(frame) return end
local leftInfo = UIPanelWindows[leftFrame:GetName()] local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if not centerFrame then -- If neither is pushable, replace (l.729-732 — the gossip<->merchant case). if leftInfo.pushable == 0 and info.pushable == 0 then SetLeftFrame(frame) return end -- Highest priority goes to center (l.735-741). if leftInfo.pushable > info.pushable then MovePanelToCenter() SetLeftFrame(frame) else SetCenterFrame(frame) end return end
-- Center is already taken too (l.744-751). local centerInfo = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if info.pushable > centerInfo.pushable then MovePanelToLeft() SetCenterFrame(frame) else SetLeftFrame(frame) end end
-- HideUIPanel(frame) — UIParent.lua l.754-786, v1 left+center slice (the real fn's -- full-screen branch, l.759-763, is dropped: no full-screen row ships). function HideUIPanel(frame) if not frame or not frame:IsShown() then return end
-- l.759-763. if frame == GetFullScreenFrame() then SetFullScreenFrame(nil) return end
if frame == GetCenterFrame() then SetCenterFrame(nil) return end
if frame == GetLeftFrame() then local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() if centerFrame then local info = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if info and info.area == "left" then MovePanelToLeft() return end end SetLeftFrame(nil) return end
frame:Hide() end
-- UISpecialFrames (UIParent.lua l.52-55) — **the addon's own ESC list**, and the reason -- this stopped being "dropped: none exist yet" (decision 1206). -- -- `tinsert(UISpecialFrames, "MyFrame")` is THE 1.12 idiom for "ESC should close my -- window", and it is 34 call sites across the corpus. With the table absent that line is -- `bad argument #1 to 'tinsert' (table expected, got nil)` — which killed 11 addons at -- load, the second-largest wall in the survey after the Lua-5.0 generic-for. -- -- Seeded with the reference's own two entries — **both** of them now. 1206 seeded only -- `ItemRefTooltip`, and its Rejected section wrote down why, verbatim: *"Listing -- `ColorPickerFrame`. The reference seeds it; we do not ship one, and a name that resolves -- to nothing is skipped harmlessly — but seeding a frame we lack would be writing a claim -- we cannot honour."* ColorPickerFrame.xml ships it, so the claim is honourable now, and -- the entry is the reference's own rather than one of ours. -- -- Note it does NOT contradict the paragraph above (our own escapable toplevels stay -- hard-listed in the ESC chain). The concern there is an addon's `tremove` breaking the -- CLIENT's own ESC; here the ESC chain carries the colour picker on its own rung — and has -- to, because ESC on this window must CANCEL (restore the colour), which this walk's plain -- `Hide` cannot do. So the table entry is not what makes ESC work; it is what makes -- `CloseWindows` put the picker away when something ELSE closes the world's windows — -- opening the game menu, a `CloseAllWindows()` — which is exactly the reference's own -- behaviour on that path, cancel-less Hide and all. UISpecialFrames = { "ItemRefTooltip", "ColorPickerFrame" }
-- CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) — UIParent.lua l.928-957. The doublewide slice stays dropped -- (we have none); the UISpecialFrames loop at l.947-954 is now carried. function CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) local leftFrame = GetLeftFrame() local centerFrame = GetCenterFrame() local fullScreenFrame = GetFullScreenFrame() local found = leftFrame or centerFrame or fullScreenFrame
HideUIPanel(leftFrame) HideUIPanel(fullScreenFrame) if centerFrame then local info = UIPanelWindows[centerFrame:GetName()] if not info or info.area ~= "center" or not ignoreCenter then HideUIPanel(centerFrame) end end
-- The special frames, the reference's own loop (l.947-954): a plain Hide, never -- HideUIPanel, because these hold no panel slot. Its `for index, value in -- UISpecialFrames do` is Lua 5.0's iterator-less generic-for, which our VM cannot run -- (decision 1202) — `ipairs` is the same walk in the dialect we have. for _, name in ipairs(UISpecialFrames) do local frame = getglobal(name) if frame and frame:IsVisible() then frame:Hide() found = 1 end end
return found end
-- CloseAllWindows(ignoreCenter) — UIParent.lua l.970-982. The real fn first loops -- ContainerFrame1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES to hide any open bags, then calls CloseWindows() for -- the panel slots, returning whether anything closed. benilla ships a single backpack window -- (BenillaBagFrame, decision 0068 T2), so that loop collapses to hiding it. The bag is NOT a -- UIPanel (no slot registration) — it must be closed here explicitly, exactly as the real -- client closes its ContainerFrames outside the slot system. Naming BenillaBagFrame here -- mirrors UIParent.lua naming ContainerFrame in the very same function. -- The five bag windows (the real fn's ContainerFrame1..NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES): the backpack -- plus the four equipped-bag windows. Chunk-LOCAL rather than BagFrame.xml's own -- BENILLA_BAG_WINDOWS global, so every user below stays nil-safe on a surface without the -- bag file (a headless panel test) — each still resolves per window through `getglobal`. -- (It was three identical inline copies until the game menu needed a fourth.) local BAG_WINDOWS = { "BenillaBagFrame", "BenillaBagFrame1", "BenillaBagFrame2", "BenillaBagFrame3", "BenillaBagFrame4" } -- ESC closes the KEYRING too, but nothing else here does. The ref's split, exactly: its -- CloseAllWindows loops every ContainerFrame and hides whatever is shown (the keyring -- included), while CloseAllBags/OpenBackpack/CloseBackpack are id-driven over the real bags -- and never see container -2 (decision 0765). So the keyring is appended for the ESC path -- alone — a vendor opening your bags must not open your keyring with them. local ESC_CLOSES = { "BenillaBagFrame", "BenillaBagFrame1", "BenillaBagFrame2", "BenillaBagFrame3", "BenillaBagFrame4", "BenillaKeyRingFrame" }
function CloseAllWindows(ignoreCenter) local bagsVisible = nil -- Hide every open bag window. Now that 'B' opens all bags at once (BagFrame.xml -- BenillaBagToggle_OnClick), ESC must close all of them, not just the backpack. The bag -- windows are NOT UIPanels (no slot registration) — they must be closed here explicitly, -- exactly as the real client closes its ContainerFrames outside the slot system. for _, name in ipairs(ESC_CLOSES) do local bag = getglobal(name) if bag and bag:IsShown() then bag:Hide() bagsVisible = 1 end end local windowsVisible = CloseWindows(ignoreCenter) return bagsVisible or windowsVisible end
-- CloseAllBags() — the ref ContainerFrame.lua l.702-707 (`CloseBackpack()` + `CloseBag(1..N)`), -- called by ShowUIPanel's native-center branch above. Distinct from CloseBackpack below on -- purpose: this is the UNCONDITIONAL close (the ref's CloseBag ignores the was-open memory), -- because a center frame takes the whole screen — nothing is being "restored afterwards" -- the way a vendor window restores the bags it opened. function CloseAllBags() for _, name in ipairs(BAG_WINDOWS) do local bag = getglobal(name) if bag and bag:IsShown() then bag:Hide() end end end
-- OpenBackpack / CloseBackpack — the real ContainerFrame.lua globals (l.187-217) the -- vendor/bank/mail/trade windows call from their OnShow/OnHide so your bags open with them -- (playing igBackPackOpen/Close alongside the window's own panel sound — the two "go -- together"), and you can sell/deposit from the open bag. Homed here in benilla's panel-glue -- file (rather than the bag's own, as in the real client) so every window that opens can call -- them regardless of FrameXML load order — the windows are looked up by name. The real fn -- tracks `backpackWasOpen` so a bag you already had open is LEFT open on the window's close; -- benilla stores that on each frame (`wasOpen`). benilla DIVERGES from the ref here on -- purpose: the real OpenBackpack touches only the backpack, but ours opens EVERY equipped -- bag with the window (director's call — decision 0561 — matching the 'B' all-bags toggle), -- so the names keep the ref's caller contract while the body loops the five windows. Every -- step is guarded, so a surface without the bag file — a headless panel test — no-ops -- rather than erroring. function OpenBackpack() for bagId = 0, 4 do -- The backpack (bag 0) always exists; an equipped-bag window only when a bag is in -- the slot (the same existence test as BagFrame.xml's OpenAllBags). local exists = bagId == 0 or (GetContainerNumSlots and GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) > 0) local bag = exists and getglobal(BAG_WINDOWS[bagId + 1]) if bag then if bag:IsShown() then bag.wasOpen = 1 -- already open: leave it, and don't close it on window hide else bag.wasOpen = nil BenillaBagWindow_Repaint(bag) bag:Show() -- OnShow → igBackPackOpen end end end end
function CloseBackpack() for _, name in ipairs(BAG_WINDOWS) do local bag = getglobal(name) if bag and bag:IsShown() and not bag.wasOpen then bag:Hide() -- OnHide → igBackPackClose end end end
-- ToggleGameMenu(clicked) — UIParent.lua l.1465-1497, the ESCAPE binding's action -- (TOGGLEGAMEMENU), run by the host (crates/benilla ui_script/input.rs) when no EditBox -- consumed the key, and by the Main Menu micro button with `clicked = 1`. It was -- benilla's own `BenillaOnEscape` while there was no menu to open (decision 0674 retires -- that name — this IS the reference function now, and an addon-visible one). -- -- TWO behaviours in one function, which is the reference's own shape: -- · `clicked` (the micro button, l.1466-1480) — a TOGGLE. Menu up ⇒ close it; menu down ⇒ -- CloseMenus() + CloseAllWindows() first, then open. It never cancels a cast or drops a -- target: clicking a button is not "get me out of this". -- · no argument (the ESC key, l.1482-1496) — the LADDER, one eater per press, in order: -- if ( StaticPopup_EscapePressed() ) then -- elseif ( OptionsFrame:IsVisible() ) then OptionsFrameCancel:Click() -- elseif ( GameMenuFrame:IsVisible() ) then PlaySound("igMainMenuQuit"); HideUIPanel(GameMenuFrame) -- elseif ( CloseMenus() ) then -- elseif ( SpellStopCasting() ) then -- elseif ( SpellStopTargeting() ) then -- elseif ( CloseAllWindows() ) then -- l.1491 -- elseif ( ClearTarget() ) then -- else PlaySound("igMainMenuOpen"); ShowUIPanel(GameMenuFrame) -- l.1494-1495 -- The ORDER is the law (the director's two-press report, decision 0449): ESC mid-cast -- cancels the cast and ONLY the cast; the target drops on a later press once nothing -- else claims it; and only a press with NOTHING left to eat opens the menu. -- -- Every reference branch is present now (the OptionsFrame rung landed with decision -- 0950 — ours hides rather than cancel-clicks; its own comment below says why). ONE -- benilla ADDITION, ahead of everything: a held cursor item is -- dropped (ClearCursor). The cursor-item model (decision 0068 T2) has no real-client ESC -- handling to mirror — vanilla leaves the item on the cursor — so this is a deliberate -- benilla convenience (ESC as the universal "get me out" key). Guarded so it stays inert -- were the cursor slice ever absent. Three further benilla rungs sit between the popup and -- CloseMenus (stack split, world map, open mail); each is commented at its own line with -- the reference mechanism it stands in for. function ToggleGameMenu(clicked) -- Looked up rather than indexed off the global: a headless panel test loads this file -- without GameMenuFrame.xml behind it, and the reference's bare `GameMenuFrame:` would -- abort the whole chain there (the `CloseMenus and` guard two rungs down, same reason). local menu = getglobal("GameMenuFrame")
-- The micro button's toggle (l.1466-1480). Its own first move is the ref's too -- (l.1467-1469): an open options window is put away before the menu toggles. if clicked then local options = getglobal("OptionsFrame") if options and options:IsVisible() then HideUIPanel(options) end if menu and menu:IsVisible() then PlaySound("igMainMenuQuit") HideUIPanel(menu) elseif menu then if CloseMenus then CloseMenus() end CloseAllWindows() PlaySound("igMainMenuOpen") ShowUIPanel(menu) end return end
if CursorHasItem and CursorHasItem() then ClearCursor() end -- An open escapable dialog eats the ESC first (the ref's StaticPopup_EscapePressed — -- defined with the popup engine below): OnCancel(data, "clicked") + hide, but ONLY for -- hideOnEscape entries, so e.g. the DEATH release popup ignores ESC like the ref's. if StaticPopup_EscapePressed() then return end -- The colour picker next (ColorPickerFrame.xml). The reference hooks ESC on the frame -- itself (`<OnKeyDown>` l.177-184, whose ESCAPE arm is `HideUIPanel(this)` + -- `cancelFunc(previousValues)`); this engine gives plain frames no raw key events, so -- it routes through this chain exactly like the AddOns list on the next rung. -- **Cancel-CLICK, not hide** — the ref's own arm restores the previous colour, and -- clicking the real button is how the options rung below already spells this (the ref's -- `OptionsFrameCancel:Click()`), so there is one cancel path, not two. local picker = getglobal("ColorPickerFrame") if picker and picker:IsVisible() then ColorPickerCancelButton:Click() return end -- The AddOns list next (decision 1197). The reference's glue twin hooks ESC directly -- (`AddonList_OnKeyDown`, whose ESCAPE arm is `AddonList_OnCancel`); this engine gives -- plain frames no raw key events, so it routes through this shared chain like the -- stack-split spinner and the world map do. **Cancel, not hide** — ESC on that window -- means "discard what I just ticked", which is the reference's own arm and the reason -- the panel stages its edits at all. local addons = getglobal("AddonListFrame") if addons and addons:IsVisible() then AddonList_OnCancel() return end -- The options window next (l.1483-1484, live since decision 0950 — this rung sat -- unfilled while GameMenuFrame.xml's disabled buttons were the gap). The ref -- cancel-clicks (`OptionsFrameCancel:Click()`); ours hides: benilla applies changes -- live, there is no pending-change model for a Cancel to roll back, so putting the -- window away IS the whole gesture — and since 1008 that covers the Keybindings -- page too (live-commit; its OnHide hook disarms a straggling bind capture, and -- while a capsule IS armed the host's capture seam swallows ESC before this chain -- ever exists — the press becomes a BIND, 1.12's law). Looked up like the menu -- above (a headless panel test loads this file without OptionsFrame.xml behind it). local options = getglobal("OptionsFrame") if options and options:IsVisible() then HideUIPanel(options) return end -- The menu itself closes next (l.1485-1487) — before every close/cancel rung below, -- so ESC with the menu up only puts the menu away. Note the sound: closing by ESC -- plays igMainMenuQuit, the same kit the Exit Game button uses — the reference's -- choice, not a copy/paste slip here. if menu and menu:IsVisible() then PlaySound("igMainMenuQuit") HideUIPanel(menu) return end -- The stack-split spinner next (decision 0216 §6/slice 2, StackSplit.xml): the real -- client's own StackSplitFrame hooks ESC directly (its OnKeyDown, `enableKeyboard="true"`) -- — this engine has no plain-frame keyboard capture (StackSplit.xml's own header comment), -- so it routes through this shared chain instead. Just hides (StackSplitFrame_OnHide -- clears the owner's hasStackSplit flag) — no accept, matching a real Cancel click. local split = getglobal("StackSplitFrame") if split and split:IsVisible() then split:Hide() return end -- The fullscreen world map next (the ref's OnKeyDown ESCAPE arm — WorldMapFrame.xml -- l.628; ours routes through this chain since frames get no raw key events). local worldmap = getglobal("WorldMapFrame") if worldmap and worldmap:IsVisible() then -- HideUIPanel, not a bare Hide: the map holds the full-screen slot (decision 0203's -- `full` row, wired 0674), and hiding it behind the manager's back would leave the -- slot pointing at an invisible frame — which then refuses every future panel. HideUIPanel(worldmap) return end -- The open-letter toplevel (decision 0544): the ref registers OpenMailFrame in -- UISpecialFrames (UIParent.lua l.46), so ESC closes it BEFORE the mail panel itself — -- routed through this chain since this v1 drops the UISpecialFrames table. Its OnHide -- runs the taken-letter auto-delete + close sound (MailFrame.lua OpenMailFrame_OnHide). local openmail = getglobal("OpenMailFrame") if openmail and openmail:IsVisible() then HideUIPanel(openmail) return end -- The ref chain's CloseMenus leg (UIParent.lua l.1488, defined with the dropdown -- engine): an open right-click/dropdown menu closes and eats the press — BEFORE the -- cast cancel, so ESC with a menu up spares a running cast, exactly the ref order. -- Guarded like CursorHasItem above: inert when the dropdown slice isn't loaded. if CloseMenus and CloseMenus() then return end -- The ref chain's SpellStopCasting leg (UIParent.lua l.1489): ESC stops the FIRST -- of {running auto-repeat, in-flight cast} and eats the press — windows close on -- the NEXT press, exactly the reference order. A CHANNEL doesn't answer (nil): the -- ref's 0x6e6e80 can't stop one — the vanilla "/stopcasting can't stop a channel" -- quirk (wow-re esc-stopcasting.md, decision 0454) — so mid-channel the press -- falls through. Truthy only when something was actually stopped (the host's -- stoppable mirror), so an idle ESC still falls through to CloseAllWindows. if SpellStopCasting() then return end -- The ref chain's SpellStopTargeting leg (UIParent.lua l.1490, decision 0792): ESC -- with the ground-targeting cursor up cancels the targeting — word cleared, no -- packet — and eats the press. After the cast rung, exactly the artifact's order -- (while merely targeting nothing is in flight, so SpellStopCasting answered nil). if SpellStopTargeting() then return end -- CloseAllWindows eats the press when it closed anything (l.1491); only a press with -- nothing left to close reaches ClearTarget (l.1492) — the ref's last eater, and the -- ONLY route to the target drop: the raw-key Esc clear the app used to run beside -- this chain double-fired on the first press (decision 0449 retires it). if CloseAllWindows() then return end if ClearTarget() then return end -- Nothing left to eat (l.1493-1495): the press opens the menu. ClearTarget answering -- nil is what gets us here — which is why its `1`/nil return is load-bearing, and why -- the ladder above must never return an unconditional truthy. if menu then PlaySound("igMainMenuOpen") ShowUIPanel(menu) end end
-- SetDesaturation(texture, desaturation) — ref UIParent.lua l.1499-1510, verbatim. The -- reference itself has a no-shader fallback, and OURS IS ALWAYS THAT PATH: this engine has -- no SetDesaturated, so `shaderSupported` is false exactly as on a 1.12 card without the -- desaturation shader, and the grey comes from the ref's own vertex-colour branch. Written -- as the wrapper rather than open-coded at each call site so the day a real desaturation -- lands, one function changes. First caller here is the game menu's bag-bar greying -- (decision 0674); PartyFrame.xml's disconnected-member branch has been CALLING this -- global since decision 0434 with nothing defining it — an error thrown every time a party -- member went offline, which is why it went unnoticed. function SetDesaturation(texture, desaturation) if not texture then return end local shaderSupported = texture.SetDesaturated and texture:SetDesaturated(desaturation) if not shaderSupported then if desaturation then texture:SetVertexColor(0.5, 0.5, 0.5) else texture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) end end end
-- ── The shared dialog IS the ref's StaticPopup engine (decision 0308 §3) ───────────────── -- Transcribed from the patch-chain StaticPopup.lua (mpqx extraction, decision 0246): -- the StaticPopupDialogs registry + StaticPopup_Show(which, arg1, arg2) + the OnUpdate -- countdown/StartDelay machinery — the death arc's dialogs exercise nearly all of it, and -- StaticPopup_Show/StaticPopupDialogs are 1.14 addon-API surface (0068). v1 scope: -- · TWO dialog instances (STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS = 2; the ref runs 4) — the deepest -- nesting exercised so far is decline-res re-showing DEATH (Show precedes the click's -- hide, so a free second instance is required). Grow toward 4 when a third coexists. -- · info fields honored: text, button1, button2, DisplayButton2, OnShow(data), -- OnHide(data), OnAccept(data, data2) (truthy return = keep open — RECOVER_CORPSE -- waits for the server, XP_LOSS's first Accept re-asks), OnCancel(data, reason) -- (reason ∈ "clicked"|"timeout"|"override"), OnUpdate(elapsed, dialog), timeout, -- StartDelay, delayText, sound, whileDead, hideOnEscape, cancels, showAlert (the -- 420 widen + DialogAlertIcon, decision 1068). -- · hasEditBox + maxLetters + EditBoxOnEnterPressed are live (decision 0668's -- ADD_FRIEND/ADD_IGNORE are the first customers): the box shows, caps its length, -- opens empty, and re-anchors the buttons under itself. -- · Accepted but v1-inert: exclusive, interruptCinematic (cinematics are acked -- instantly — 0196), notClosableByLogout, preferredIndex, hasWideEditBox (guild -- MOTD/notes — the guild arc), and the money variant. -- · text_arg1/2 stash on the DIALOG frame (the ref stashes them on the Text region; -- our regions don't carry Lua fields). -- · GetText("SECONDS"/"MINUTES") localization collapses to English singular/plural. -- · Button widths stay the template's fixed 120 (the ref widens past 120/110 via -- GetTextWidth; the widen law joins when a longer label first needs it). -- · Resize runs per tick while shown, not only on text swaps: GetHeight's measure has a -- frame of latency (the measured-width convention below), so the height self-corrects -- the frame after any text change. STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS = 2 StaticPopupDialogs = {}
local function StaticPopupTimeUnit(n, minutes) if minutes then if n == 1 then return "minute" end return "minutes" end if n == 1 then return "second" end return "seconds" end
function StaticPopup_FindVisible(which) for index = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. index) if frame:IsShown() and frame.which == which then return frame end end return nil end
-- Ref l.1870-1877 (returns the frame NAME — the ref's contract). function StaticPopup_Visible(which) local frame = StaticPopup_FindVisible(which) if frame then return frame:GetName() end return nil end
function StaticPopup_Hide(which) for index = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. index) if frame:IsShown() and frame.which == which then frame:Hide() end end end
-- Ref l.1428-1438, the no-editbox/no-money leg only (v1 has neither variant). function StaticPopup_Resize(dialog, which) local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") local button1 = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button1") local editBox = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "EditBox") if StaticPopupDialogs[which] and StaticPopupDialogs[which].hasEditBox then dialog:SetHeight(16 + text:GetHeight() + 8 + editBox:GetHeight() + 8 + button1:GetHeight() + 16) else dialog:SetHeight(16 + text:GetHeight() + 8 + button1:GetHeight() + 16) end end
-- Ref l.1441-1700. Returns the dialog, or nil when refused (whileDead gate / no free -- instance) — calling info.OnCancel() on refusal exactly as the ref does. function StaticPopup_Show(which, text_arg1, text_arg2, data) local info = StaticPopupDialogs[which] if not info then return nil end
-- The whileDead gate (ref l.1447-1452). UnitIsDeadOrGhost lands with the death arc's -- ghost predicate — guarded like CursorHasItem in ToggleGameMenu until then. if UnitIsDeadOrGhost and UnitIsDeadOrGhost("player") and not info.whileDead then if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel() end return nil end
-- Showing X hides a visible X.cancels with an "override" cancel (ref l.1470-1485). if info.cancels then local frame = StaticPopup_FindVisible(info.cancels) if frame then frame:Hide() local OnCancel = StaticPopupDialogs[frame.which].OnCancel if OnCancel then OnCancel(frame.data, "override") end end end
-- Showing DEATH sweeps every visible non-whileDead dialog (ref l.1501-1512). if which == "DEATH" then for index = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. index) if frame:IsShown() and not StaticPopupDialogs[frame.which].whileDead then frame:Hide() local OnCancel = StaticPopupDialogs[frame.which].OnCancel if OnCancel then OnCancel(frame.data, "override") end end end end
-- A visible same-type dialog is overridden in place; else take a free instance -- (ref l.1515-1553). local dialog = StaticPopup_FindVisible(which) if dialog then if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel(dialog.data, "override") end dialog:Hide() end if not dialog then for i = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. i) if not frame:IsShown() then dialog = frame break end end end if not dialog then if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel() end return nil end
-- The text. Countdown/delay dialogs start blank — their OnUpdate writes it -- (ref l.1556-1574's which-list, verbatim). local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") if (which == "DEATH") or (which == "CAMP") or (which == "QUIT") or (which == "DUEL_OUTOFBOUNDS") or (which == "RECOVER_CORPSE") or (which == "RESURRECT") or (which == "RESURRECT_NO_SICKNESS") or (which == "INSTANCE_BOOT") or (which == "CONFIRM_SUMMON") or (which == "AREA_SPIRIT_HEAL") then text:SetText(" ") dialog.text_arg1 = text_arg1 dialog.text_arg2 = text_arg2 else text:SetText(format(info.text, text_arg1, text_arg2)) end
-- The alert dress (ref l.1579-1589): every Show resets width 320 / icon hidden, then -- a showAlert entry widens to 420 and shows the icon. The ref's neighbouring arms — -- the guild-MOTD 420 widen and HELP_TICKET's 350 — wait for their dialogs. local alertIcon = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "AlertIcon") alertIcon:Hide() dialog:SetWidth(320) if info.showAlert then dialog:SetWidth(420) alertIcon:Show() end
-- The edit box (ref l.1599-1624): shown only for a hasEditBox entry, capped at the -- entry's maxLetters, and always empty on open — a name left over from the last time -- the dialog ran would be sent by a reflexive Enter. The wide variant is guild-only -- (MOTD/notes), so it waits for the guild arc. local editBox = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "EditBox") if info.hasEditBox then editBox:SetMaxLetters(info.maxLetters or 0) editBox:SetText("") editBox:Show() else editBox:Hide() end
-- The buttons (ref l.1634-1676; fixed 120 widths — header note). Button2 shows only -- when the entry names it AND DisplayButton2 (when present) allows it; a solo button1 -- re-seats centered under the text. With an edit box the pair hangs off the BOX's -- bottom instead of the text's (ref l.1641-1643), which is what leaves room for it. local buttonAnchor = info.hasEditBox and (dialog:GetName() .. "EditBox") or (dialog:GetName() .. "Text") local button1 = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button1") local button2 = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button2") if info.button2 and (not info.DisplayButton2 or info.DisplayButton2()) then button1:ClearAllPoints() button2:ClearAllPoints() button1:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", buttonAnchor, "BOTTOM", -6, -8) button2:SetPoint("LEFT", dialog:GetName() .. "Button1", "RIGHT", 13, 0) button2:SetText(info.button2) button2:Show() else button1:ClearAllPoints() button1:SetPoint("TOP", buttonAnchor, "BOTTOM", 0, -8) button2:Hide() end if info.button1 then button1:SetText(info.button1) button1:Show() else button1:Hide() end
-- Misc vars (ref l.1677-1690). `which` is set before Show so OnShow reads it. dialog.which = which dialog.timeleft = info.timeout or 0 dialog.hideOnEscape = info.hideOnEscape dialog.data = data
if info.StartDelay then dialog.startDelay = info.StartDelay() button1:Disable() else dialog.startDelay = nil button1:Enable() end
dialog:Show() StaticPopup_Resize(dialog, which)
if info.sound then PlaySound(info.sound) end return dialog end
-- Ref l.1850-1868: a truthy OnAccept return keeps the dialog open. function StaticPopup_OnClick(dialog, index) local which = dialog.which local info = StaticPopupDialogs[which] if not info then return end local dontHide = nil if index == 1 then if info.OnAccept then dontHide = info.OnAccept(dialog.data, dialog.data2) end else if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel(dialog.data, "clicked") end end if not dontHide and (which == dialog.which) then dialog:Hide() end end
-- The edit box's two keys (ref StaticPopup.xml's template scripts). Enter runs the -- entry's EditBoxOnEnterPressed hook, which by convention does the accept work and hides -- the dialog itself; Escape dismisses the dialog through the ordinary cancel path so a -- half-typed name never acts. function StaticPopup_EditBoxOnEnterPressed(editBox) local dialog = editBox:GetParent() local info = StaticPopupDialogs[dialog.which] if info and info.EditBoxOnEnterPressed then info.EditBoxOnEnterPressed(dialog.data) end end
function StaticPopup_EditBoxOnEscapePressed(editBox) local dialog = editBox:GetParent() editBox:ClearFocus() dialog:Hide() end
-- Ref l.1832-1848: the open/close pair sounds on EVERY path, then the entry's own hook. function StaticPopup_OnShow() PlaySound("igMainMenuOpen") local info = StaticPopupDialogs[this.which] if info and info.OnShow then info.OnShow(this.data) end end
function StaticPopup_OnHide() PlaySound("igMainMenuClose") local info = StaticPopupDialogs[this.which] if info and info.OnHide then info.OnHide(this.data) end end
-- Ref l.1712-1808: the timeout countdown (expiry → OnCancel "timeout" + hide), the -- per-tick countdown text for the timer dialogs, the StartDelay gate (button1 disabled, -- delayText counts down, then the real text swaps in and the button enables), then the -- entry's own OnUpdate. The INSTANCE_BOOT/CONFIRM_SUMMON special text formats join with -- their dialogs; their which-list slots stay so the gate is the ref's. function StaticPopup_OnUpdate(dialog, elapsed) local info = StaticPopupDialogs[dialog.which] if not info then return end if (dialog.timeleft or 0) > 0 then local which = dialog.which local timeleft = dialog.timeleft - elapsed if timeleft <= 0 then dialog.timeleft = 0 if info.OnCancel then info.OnCancel(dialog.data, "timeout") end dialog:Hide() return end dialog.timeleft = timeleft
if (which == "DEATH") or (which == "CAMP") or (which == "QUIT") or (which == "DUEL_OUTOFBOUNDS") or (which == "INSTANCE_BOOT") or (which == "CONFIRM_SUMMON") or (which == "AREA_SPIRIT_HEAL") then local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") timeleft = ceil(timeleft) if timeleft < 60 then text:SetText(format(info.text, timeleft, StaticPopupTimeUnit(timeleft, false))) else local m = ceil(timeleft / 60) text:SetText(format(info.text, m, StaticPopupTimeUnit(m, true))) end end end if dialog.startDelay then local which = dialog.which local timeleft = dialog.startDelay - elapsed if timeleft <= 0 then dialog.startDelay = nil local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") text:SetText(format(info.text, dialog.text_arg1, dialog.text_arg2)) getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Button1"):Enable() return end dialog.startDelay = timeleft
if (which == "RECOVER_CORPSE") or (which == "RESURRECT") or (which == "RESURRECT_NO_SICKNESS") then local text = getglobal(dialog:GetName() .. "Text") timeleft = ceil(timeleft) if (which == "RESURRECT") or (which == "RESURRECT_NO_SICKNESS") then if timeleft < 60 then text:SetText(format(info.delayText, dialog.text_arg1, timeleft, StaticPopupTimeUnit(timeleft, false))) else local m = ceil(timeleft / 60) text:SetText(format(info.delayText, dialog.text_arg1, m, StaticPopupTimeUnit(m, true))) end else if timeleft < 60 then text:SetText(format(info.delayText, timeleft, StaticPopupTimeUnit(timeleft, false))) else local m = ceil(timeleft / 60) text:SetText(format(info.delayText, m, StaticPopupTimeUnit(m, true))) end end end end StaticPopup_Resize(dialog, dialog.which) if info.OnUpdate then info.OnUpdate(elapsed, dialog) end end
-- Ref l.1879-1893: only hideOnEscape dialogs respond — a shown DEATH popup deliberately -- does NOT close on ESC. Returns truthy when something closed (the caller's chain stops). function StaticPopup_EscapePressed() local closed = nil for index = 1, STATICPOPUP_NUMDIALOGS do local frame = getglobal("StaticPopup" .. index) if frame:IsShown() and frame.hideOnEscape then local OnCancel = StaticPopupDialogs[frame.which].OnCancel if OnCancel then OnCancel(frame.data, "clicked") end frame:Hide() closed = 1 end end return closed end
-- Delete-item confirm strings — the real 1.12 GlobalStrings.lua (patch-2.MPQ, -- Interface\FrameXML\GlobalStrings.lua), quoted verbatim (extracted via benilla-extract). local DELETE_ITEM_TEXT = "Do you want to destroy %s?" -- DELETE_ITEM; %s = the item name local YES_TEXT = "Yes" -- YES local NO_TEXT = "No" -- No
-- Ref StaticPopup.lua l.659-679, verbatim — its own OnUpdate poll (cursor emptied by any -- other path → hide) replaces the old bespoke `deleteItemFlow` CURSOR_UPDATE driver. -- exclusive is v1-inert (engine header note); showAlert is live since 1068 — the ref's -- own "display the error image" case is this very dialog. StaticPopupDialogs["DELETE_ITEM"] = { text = DELETE_ITEM_TEXT, button1 = YES_TEXT, button2 = NO_TEXT, OnAccept = function() DeleteCursorItem() end, OnCancel = function() ClearCursor() end, OnUpdate = function() if not CursorHasItem() then StaticPopup_Hide("DELETE_ITEM") end end, timeout = 0, whileDead = 1, exclusive = 1, showAlert = 1, hideOnEscape = 1, }

DEFERRED (0216 §3): the ref splits quality >= 3 to -- DELETE_GOOD_ITEM (the typed-confirmation editbox variant) — no editbox variant yet, so -- every quality (arg2) shows DELETE_ITEM for now. function BenillaDeleteItemConfirmDriver_OnEvent(frame) if event == "DELETE_ITEM_CONFIRM" then StaticPopup_Show("DELETE_ITEM", arg1) end end
-- ── The shared frame-fade kit — ref UIParent.lua:1103-1219, transcribed VERBATIM (the -- while-index iteration included; tinsert/tDeleteItem spelled as table.insert / the -- remove loop). The ref drives UIFrameFadeUpdate from UIParent's OnUpdate; our driver is -- the BenillaFadeDriver frame below. Callers: the quest detail write-on -- (QuestFrame.xml) fades TextAlphaDependentFrame in over QUESTINFO_FADE_IN. ────────────── FADEFRAMES = {}
function UIFrameFadeRemoveFrame(frame) local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do if FADEFRAMES[index] == frame then table.remove(FADEFRAMES, index) else index = index + 1 end end end
function UIFrameFade(frame, fadeInfo) if not fadeInfo.mode then fadeInfo.mode = "IN" end if fadeInfo.mode == "IN" then if not fadeInfo.startAlpha then fadeInfo.startAlpha = 0 end if not fadeInfo.endAlpha then fadeInfo.endAlpha = 1.0 end elseif fadeInfo.mode == "OUT" then if not fadeInfo.startAlpha then fadeInfo.startAlpha = 1.0 end if not fadeInfo.endAlpha then fadeInfo.endAlpha = 0 end end frame:SetAlpha(fadeInfo.startAlpha) frame.fadeInfo = fadeInfo -- Already fading? Leave the running fade alone (the ref's early return). local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do if FADEFRAMES[index] == frame then return end index = index + 1 end frame:Show() table.insert(FADEFRAMES, frame) end
function UIFrameFadeIn(frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) local fadeInfo = {} fadeInfo.mode = "IN" fadeInfo.timeToFade = timeToFade fadeInfo.startAlpha = startAlpha fadeInfo.endAlpha = endAlpha UIFrameFade(frame, fadeInfo) end
function UIFrameFadeOut(frame, timeToFade, startAlpha, endAlpha) local fadeInfo = {} fadeInfo.mode = "OUT" fadeInfo.timeToFade = timeToFade fadeInfo.startAlpha = startAlpha fadeInfo.endAlpha = endAlpha UIFrameFade(frame, fadeInfo) end
function UIFrameFadeUpdate(elapsed) local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do local frame = FADEFRAMES[index] local fadeInfo = frame.fadeInfo if not fadeInfo.fadeTimer then fadeInfo.fadeTimer = 0 end fadeInfo.fadeTimer = fadeInfo.fadeTimer + elapsed if fadeInfo.fadeTimer < fadeInfo.timeToFade then if fadeInfo.mode == "IN" then frame:SetAlpha((fadeInfo.fadeTimer / fadeInfo.timeToFade) * (fadeInfo.endAlpha - fadeInfo.startAlpha) + fadeInfo.startAlpha) elseif fadeInfo.mode == "OUT" then frame:SetAlpha(((fadeInfo.timeToFade - fadeInfo.fadeTimer) / fadeInfo.timeToFade) * (fadeInfo.startAlpha - fadeInfo.endAlpha) + fadeInfo.endAlpha) end else frame:SetAlpha(fadeInfo.endAlpha) if fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime and fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime > 0 then fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime = fadeInfo.fadeHoldTime - elapsed else UIFrameFadeRemoveFrame(frame) if fadeInfo.finishedFunc then fadeInfo.finishedFunc(fadeInfo.finishedArg1, fadeInfo.finishedArg2, fadeInfo.finishedArg3, fadeInfo.finishedArg4) fadeInfo.finishedFunc = nil end end end index = index + 1 end end
function UIFrameIsFading(frame) local index = 1 while FADEFRAMES[index] do if FADEFRAMES[index] == frame then return 1 end index = index + 1 end return nil end
-- ── The tab kit (ref UIPanelTemplates.lua l.1-29/90-133, transcribed VERBATIM shape) ── -- One selected tab per group: the frame carries numTabs/selectedTab, tabs are named -- <frame>Tab1..N (CharacterFrameTabButtonTemplate instances — the template lives in this -- file). SelectTab swaps the InActive art for the Active art and disables the button (a -- selected tab doesn't re-click); DeselectTab reverses it. Omitted vs ref: the -- isDisabled/SetDisabledTabState arm (no window has a disabled tab yet) and the SelectTab -- tab-tooltip hide (our tabs set no tooltip). First consumer: the merchant's -- Merchant/Buyback pair. function PanelTemplates_SetNumTabs(frame, numTabs) frame.numTabs = numTabs end
function PanelTemplates_SetTab(frame, id) frame.selectedTab = id PanelTemplates_UpdateTabs(frame) end
function PanelTemplates_GetSelectedTab(frame) return frame.selectedTab end
function PanelTemplates_UpdateTabs(frame) if not frame.selectedTab then return end for i = 1, frame.numTabs do local tab = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Tab" .. i) if tab.isDisabled then PanelTemplates_SetDisabledTabState(tab) elseif i == frame.selectedTab then PanelTemplates_SelectTab(tab) else PanelTemplates_DeselectTab(tab) end end end
-- The disabled-tab arm (ref UIPanelTemplates.lua l.94-105 + l.135-148) — the piece this -- kit deliberately omitted until a window needed it. First customer: the social window's -- GUILD tab, which `InGuildCheck` disables for a character in no guild — i.e. permanently -- until the guild arc exists (decision 0668). A disabled tab wears the INACTIVE -- three-slice art (like an unselected tab) but is un-clickable with a greyed label, so it -- reads as "there, not for you" rather than as the selected one. function PanelTemplates_DisableTab(frame, index) getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Tab" .. index).isDisabled = 1 PanelTemplates_UpdateTabs(frame) end
function PanelTemplates_EnableTab(frame, index) local tab = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "Tab" .. index) tab.isDisabled = nil tab:SetDisabledTextColor(HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.r, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.g, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR.b) PanelTemplates_UpdateTabs(frame) end
function PanelTemplates_SetDisabledTabState(tab) local name = tab:GetName() getglobal(name .. "Left"):Show() getglobal(name .. "Middle"):Show() getglobal(name .. "Right"):Show() tab:Disable() tab.text = tab:GetText() tab:SetDisabledTextColor(GRAY_FONT_COLOR.r, GRAY_FONT_COLOR.g, GRAY_FONT_COLOR.b) getglobal(name .. "LeftDisabled"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "RightDisabled"):Hide() end
function PanelTemplates_DeselectTab(tab) local name = tab:GetName() getglobal(name .. "Left"):Show() getglobal(name .. "Middle"):Show() getglobal(name .. "Right"):Show() tab:Enable() getglobal(name .. "LeftDisabled"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "RightDisabled"):Hide() end
function PanelTemplates_SelectTab(tab) local name = tab:GetName() getglobal(name .. "Left"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "Middle"):Hide() getglobal(name .. "Right"):Hide() tab:Disable() getglobal(name .. "LeftDisabled"):Show() getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):Show() getglobal(name .. "RightDisabled"):Show() end
-- The text-fit (ref PanelTemplates_TabResize, UIPanelTemplates.lua l.31-88 — now the WHOLE -- function, `(padding, tab, absoluteSize, maxWidth)`): the tab is text + padding wide, plus -- the two end slices; both middle slices stretch to the text; the text box itself un-sizes -- to natural. `maxWidth` CAPS it and pins the label's box to the cap instead — the arm that -- keeps a long tab inside its window, which the first transcription dropped and the macro -- window's character tab then overran (0983 → 0991). `absoluteSize` is the ref's third arm, -- transcribed with it so the next caller has it. -- -- One deviation: the ref reads the label's laid-out GetWidth (its C measure is synchronous); -- ours reads GetStringWidth — the same number once the measure round-trip lands, which is -- why the caller below re-checks from OnUpdate instead of OnShow. function PanelTemplates_TabResize(padding, tab, absoluteSize, maxWidth) local name = tab:GetName() local text = getglobal(name .. "Text") local sideWidths = 2 * getglobal(name .. "Left"):GetWidth() local width, tabWidth if absoluteSize then if absoluteSize < sideWidths then width, tabWidth = 1, sideWidths else width, tabWidth = absoluteSize - sideWidths, absoluteSize end text:SetWidth(width) else width = text:GetStringWidth() + (padding or 24) if maxWidth and width > maxWidth then width = maxWidth + (padding or 24) text:SetWidth(width) else text:SetWidth(0) end tabWidth = width + sideWidths end getglobal(name .. "Middle"):SetWidth(width) getglobal(name .. "MiddleDisabled"):SetWidth(width) tab:SetWidth(tabWidth) -- benilla addition: hand back the width just declared. `tab:GetWidth()` cannot serve -- it — that reads the last RESOLVED rect, which inside a settle is this frame's stale -- input, not the value one line above just set. A clamp that read it back saw the old -- width, declined to fire, and the settle's gate then locked the un-clamped result in -- for good (decision 1002). return tabWidth end
-- The tab template's per-frame settle: the ref does TabResize(0) once, in OnShow -- (CharacterFrameTemplates.xml l.77-80), trusting a synchronous text measure. Our -- GetStringWidth has a frame of latency, so the template's OnUpdate calls this until the -- measured width settles (then it's a no-op compare per frame). The ref sizes the hover -- highlight alongside it; this kit does not — both tab templates anchor their highlight to -- their own side edges, so it is the tab by construction and no settle can desync it -- (decision 1004). -- -- The fit PARAMETERS live on the tab (`benillaTabPadding`/`benillaTabMaxWidth`, defaulting -- to the +0 fit every window tab has always used) rather than at the call site, because -- there is exactly one call site and it is this settle loop: an instance that ran its own -- TabResize in OnLoad — as the reference's macro tabs do — would just be overwritten on the -- next frame. Setting the two fields IS how an instance asks for the reference's own fit. -- THE STRUCTURAL CLAMP — a tab may never grow past its window's drawn right edge, whatever -- the instance asked for (decision 1002; the director's "fix this properly to prevent it -- ever again"). The reference's own caps are numbers hand-tuned to ITS font: the macro -- window's 150 is right for the enUS FRIZQT__ the 1.12 client rasterizes and for nothing -- else in particular, and the label it guards carries a CHARACTER NAME — the one string -- whose width no window author can know. So the instance's cap is a preference and the -- window's edge is the law. -- -- `benillaTabRightInset` is how a window declares how far its DRAWN plate stops short of -- its frame rect, because no kit can introspect an art margin. The macro window's is 40: -- its 384-unit frame is painted by a 256-wide slice plus a 128-wide one that carries a -- transparent tail. Clamping to the frame rect instead — the first attempt — clamped to a -- boundary the player cannot see, and the tab still walked out over the world. -- -- The clamp is applied to the RESULT, through TabResize's own `absoluteSize` arm, rather -- than folded into `maxWidth`: that parameter is compared against `text + padding` but -- assigned as `maxWidth + padding`, so a room budget expressed through it is off by the -- padding and silently fails to bind. `absoluteSize` sets the tab width outright, which is -- exactly what a room budget is. function BenillaTab_Room(tab) local parent = tab:GetParent() if not parent then return nil end local left, right = tab:GetLeft(), parent:GetRight() if not left or not right then return nil end local room = (right - (tab.benillaTabRightInset or 0)) - left if room < 1 then room = 1 end return room end
function BenillaTabButton_OnUpdate(tab) local text = getglobal(tab:GetName() .. "Text") local w = (text and text:GetStringWidth()) or 0 if w <= 0 then return end local pad = tab.benillaTabPadding or 0 local room = BenillaTab_Room(tab) if tab.benillaFitWidth == w and tab.benillaFitRoom == room then return end tab.benillaFitWidth, tab.benillaFitRoom = w, room local fitted = PanelTemplates_TabResize(pad, tab, nil, tab.benillaTabMaxWidth) if room and fitted > room then PanelTemplates_TabResize(pad, tab, room) end -- No highlight sizing here on purpose — BOTH tab templates anchor their highlight to -- their own two side edges, so it IS the tab by construction (decision 1004). end
